parts.note: a moonlight flit is a secret night-time escape from unpaid rent; the garment meant is an old word for a nightgown, a shift worn at night

explanation.surface: Someone wonders what to wear when sneaking off by night.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'moonlight flit' is British slang for leaving a lodging at night to dodge the rent. A night-shift is an old name for a nightdress, and the second reading is a work rota run in the dark hours.
explanation.definitionFit: A shift was a plain chemise, so one worn in bed is a nightgown; such garments suit a nocturnal getaway.

clue.text: Like Collins's book which shall be this ?

definitions.text: Like Collins's book which shall be this

parts.words: Like Collins's book which shall be this
parts.note: Wilkie Collins wrote the novel No Name, and a person 'who shall be' unnamed is in the stock phrase

explanation.surface: A novel by Collins whose title must stay secret.
explanation.walkthrough: Wilkie Collins's novel is 'No Name'; the phrase 'a name which shall be nameless' completes the second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Without a name, as the title of Collins's novel declares.

parts.note: people who live well and eat well, with a nod to the Swiss bankers called the gnomes of Zurich

explanation.surface: Wealthy residents enjoying life in Zurich.
explanation.walkthrough: Zurich's bankers were famously called 'the gnomes of Zurich'; the answer ends in a word sounding like gnomes.
explanation.definitionFit: Connoisseurs of fine food live well, and the word's ending recalls Swiss financiers.

clue.text: French painter can put up a good performance on Shrove Tuesday

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting up means the words are written upwards, bottom to top

parts.words: a good performance on Shrove Tuesday
parts.note: tossing the pancake is the feat expected on Pancake Day

explanation.surface: A French artist shows off his pancake skills on Shrove Tuesday.
explanation.walkthrough: Shrove Tuesday is Pancake Day in Britain, when pancakes are tossed; 'put up' reverses TOSS IT. James Tissot was a French painter.
explanation.definitionFit: James Tissot was a nineteenth-century French artist known for society scenes.

parts.note: Sir Jack, the great Surrey and England opening batsman

explanation.surface: A man named Jack representing England.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Jack Hobbs was an England cricketer, the leading run scorer in first-class history.
explanation.definitionFit: A celebrated opening batsman for England between the wars bore this surname.

clue.text: Where elbow grease is wanted ; that sounds somewhat humorous

definitions.meaning: the tender spot at the elbow, which a bump makes tingle
the arm bone, the humerus, is said like humorous

explanation.surface: Hard work is needed, though that seems funny.
explanation.definitionFit: The nerve at the elbow lies by the humerus, whose name echoes a word for comic.

parts.note: the fixed salaries paid to clergy

explanation.surface: Salaries paid to government ministers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ministerial' suggests government, but the minister is a clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: Clergy are paid a fixed allowance rather than a wage.

parts.note: the unit of electrical current, the ampere, is usually written in a shortened form

explanation.surface: Someone is running low on cash or on electricity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short of' suggests lacking, but here it means an abbreviation: the clipped name of the unit measuring current.
explanation.definitionFit: The ampere is the unit of electrical current, commonly abbreviated in speech and writing.

parts.note: the Welsh folk song is named after a grove of a certain tree

explanation.surface: A wood where choirs perform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Ash Grove' is a well-known Welsh folk song.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional Welsh song names a grove of this tree.

parts.note: seated as a model is for an artist, set in place for a sitting

explanation.surface: Seated like a fashion model.
explanation.definitionFit: A model sits still in a set position for a painter, as if set on a throne.

parts.note: the nine goddesses of the arts gave their name to the museum, the first gallery

explanation.surface: Girls who first hung around art galleries.
explanation.walkthrough: The museum takes its name from the Greek Mouseion, a shrine to the nine goddesses of the arts.
explanation.definitionFit: The nine goddesses of arts and learning are the source of the word museum, so they are the first gallery's ladies.

parts.note: square means staid and old-fashioned, as a tea party is; a fight over buns would mean pulling the hair worn in a bun

explanation.surface: Respectable parties that end with guests tearing at each other's hair.
explanation.walkthrough: A bunfight is British slang for a tea party or formal gathering; read literally it is a scuffle over buns, the hairstyle, hence hair-pulling.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea parties are staid social events, colloquially named for the cakes served at them.

clue.text: Landor's inclined to put on fat in strips !

indicators.note: inclined means tilted or leaning, so the letters of the poet's name are set askew into a new order

parts.note: Walter Savage Landor, the English poet, with the possessive giving a final S

explanation.surface: The poet Landor is prone to putting on weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inclined to put on fat' reads as a tendency to gain weight, but 'inclined' is the anagram signal working on LANDORS.
explanation.definitionFit: Small strips of bacon fat are used in French cooking to enrich lean meat.

definitions.meaning: gave way, surrendered to an opponent
a field at harvest has produced its crop

explanation.surface: Someone gave up a contest just as the crops came in.
explanation.definitionFit: To give in is to surrender; a field gives its produce at harvest, so both senses mean gave.

clue.text: Descriptive of boos, cat calls, or the perfect steak ?

definitions.text: Descriptive of boos, cat calls, or the perfect steak

parts.words: Descriptive of boos, cat calls, or the perfect steak
parts.note: jeers aimed at a performer's act, and meat cooked exactly right

explanation.surface: Words for heckling, or for a well-cooked steak.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'turn' is a stage act, so heckling is aimed at it; the phrase also means cooked perfectly.
explanation.definitionFit: Cooked exactly right is the idiom; jeers are directed at a performer's act.

clue.text: " And all the season of snows and" (Swinburne)

definitions.text: " And all the season of snows and" (Swinburne)

parts.words: " And all the season of snows and" (Swinburne)
parts.note: a line from the chorus of Atalanta in Calydon, whose missing last word is wrongdoings

explanation.surface: A quotation from Swinburne with its final word left blank.
explanation.walkthrough: The line comes from Swinburne's 'Atalanta in Calydon': 'And all the season of snows and sins'.
explanation.definitionFit: The poem pairs winter's snows with transgressions, the word that completes the alliterative line.

indicators.note: taken as there is a scramble of the following words, the phrase points to rearranging fun, in and gold together

explanation.surface: Unwrapping a gift turns out to be fun when gold is inside.
explanation.walkthrough: The nine letters of FUN, IN and GOLD are rearranged; the surface reads as a pleasure in finding gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Opening out something folded displays what was concealed, so it exposes it.

parts.note: Franklin Roosevelt's policy of friendly relations with Latin America

explanation.surface: A fine policy of President Roosevelt.
explanation.walkthrough: FDR's Good Neighbor Policy sought friendly relations with Latin America.
explanation.definitionFit: Roosevelt's Latin American policy was named for being a friendly person next door.

clue.text: " They flash upon that inward eye Which is the bliss of" (Wordsworth)

definitions.text: " They flash upon that inward eye Which is the bliss of" (Wordsworth)

parts.words: " They flash upon that inward eye Which is the bliss of" (Wordsworth)
parts.note: the daffodils poem ends its line with a word for being alone

explanation.surface: A quotation from Wordsworth with its last word left blank.
explanation.walkthrough: From Wordsworth's 'I Wandered Lonely as a Cloud': 'Which is the bliss of solitude'.
explanation.definitionFit: The poet's remembered daffodils delight him when alone, completing the line.

clue.text: Is it doing time that ages them, the geese ?

definitions.text: Is it doing time that ages them, the geese

parts.words: Is it doing time that ages them, the geese
parts.note: lags are convicts doing time, and prison might turn them grey

explanation.surface: A question whether prison makes geese look older.
explanation.walkthrough: A lag is British slang for a convict; grey lags read as prisoners turned grey by their sentence, and are also wild geese.
explanation.definitionFit: A grey wild goose of Europe is the ancestor of farmyard geese.

definitions.meaning: coiled shelled fossils named after the curled horn of the god Ammon
a people of the Old Testament, descendants of Lot living east of the Jordan

explanation.surface: Elderly men of the Old Testament still feeling amorous.
explanation.definitionFit: The spiral fossils resemble a ram's horn, and a biblical tribe shares the same name.

parts.note: each state of the USA is represented by one emblem on the American flag

explanation.surface: Something that signals the president's annual address.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State of the Union' suggests the presidential speech, but here it is one state among the fifty, each marked on the US flag.
explanation.definitionFit: The Stars and Stripes carries one five-pointed emblem per member state.

parts.note: Harry, author of Ruthless Rhymes for Heartless Homes

explanation.surface: A merciless poet named Harry.
explanation.definitionFit: Harry Graham wrote the comic verse collection Ruthless Rhymes for Heartless Homes.

clue.text: Diana's chit may be only a couple of lines

parts.note: Di is the short form of Diana, with the possessive adding S

indicators.note: may be suggests the word chit could be something else once its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A note from Diana might be very brief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'May be' turns CHIT into TICH, placed after DIS.
explanation.definitionFit: A couplet of verse, two lines forming a unit, has this Greek-derived name.

parts.note: Freud analysed the night-time visions of sleep, the realm of his study

explanation.surface: Freud's home country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Land of Freud' suggests Austria, but it is the land of sleep's visions that he interpreted.
explanation.definitionFit: Freud's Interpretation of Dreams made sleep visions his domain; 'dreamland' completes it.

parts.note: roan describes a horse's coat; the North African coast gave its name to the Barb breed of horse

explanation.surface: A land of speckled horses.
explanation.walkthrough: The Barb horse comes from North Africa's old Barbary coast, so a horse-colour word points to the region.
explanation.definitionFit: The North African coast region is the home of the Barb, a famed breed of horse.

parts.note: ... slag is a fertiliser made from steelworks waste, and the first word means fundamental

explanation.surface: Something essential to rubbish talk.
explanation.walkthrough: Basic slag is a phosphate fertiliser from steelmaking; 'slag' also suggests the British slang for insulting.
explanation.definitionFit: Fundamental is a synonym, and the word precedes slag in the fertiliser's name.

clue.text: They have to translate the will into the deed !

definitions.text: They have to translate the will into the deed

parts.words: They have to translate the will into the deed
parts.note: the people named in a testament carry out its wishes, turning the document into action

explanation.surface: People who must put intentions into action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The will' reads as intention, but it is the legal testament, and 'the deed' as a legal document as well as an action.
explanation.definitionFit: Persons appointed in a testament administer the estate, carrying out the dead person's instructions.

clue.text: " Where the quiet-coloured of evening smiles " (Browning)

definitions.text: " Where the quiet-coloured of evening smiles " (Browning)

parts.words: " Where the quiet-coloured of evening smiles " (Browning)
parts.note: a line from Love Among the Ruins, the missing word meaning close or finish

explanation.surface: A quotation from Browning with a word left blank.
explanation.walkthrough: From Browning's 'Love Among the Ruins': 'Where the quiet-coloured end of evening smiles'.
explanation.definitionFit: The close of evening is its finish, the word the poet uses.

parts.note: the West African language widely spoken across northern Nigeria as a common tongue

explanation.surface: A shared language of Nigeria.
explanation.definitionFit: This Chadic language serves as a trade tongue across northern Nigeria and neighbouring states.

clue.text: These cons are pros for house-hunters

definitions.text: These cons are pros for house-hunters

parts.words: These cons are pros for house-hunters
parts.note: modern conveniences, shortened in estate agents' jargon, are advantages to buyers

explanation.surface: Drawbacks that turn out to be selling points for buyers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mod cons' is British estate-agent shorthand for modern conveniences; the clue plays on cons versus pros.
explanation.definitionFit: The shortened form of modern is paired with cons in property advertisements.

parts.note: substances that make soil richer, and also ornaments that make a thing richer

explanation.surface: Garden feeds that also look pretty.
explanation.definitionFit: Additions that improve soil, or embellishments that adorn, are both things that make richer.
